blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A settings class declares `public Boolean isArchived()` and `public void setArchived(Boolean archived)`. An admin screen built on `java.beans.Introspector` shows each property's current value and lets an operator edit it. What does the screen do with `archived`?

options.text: It shows the value and accepts edits, since both methods fit the bean naming rules for their types
options.says: Boolean isArchived() is not a getter: is names one only for a primitive boolean

options.text: It shows the value and refuses edits, since only isArchived() fits the bean naming rules for its type
options.says: it is the other way round: setArchived(Boolean) is a write method and isArchived() returning Boolean is not a getter

options.text: It accepts edits and shows no value, since only setArchived() fits the bean naming rules for its type
options.says: is names a getter only for a primitive boolean, so the property has a write method and no read method, as enabled has in the page's run

options.text: It neither shows nor accepts it, since neither method fits the bean naming rules for its type
options.says: a void setter with one parameter is a write method whatever its type, and a setter alone gives a write-only property

origin.section: Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean

questions.stem: A pool configuration class was rewritten in builder style: `public PoolConfig setMaxSize(int maxSize) { this.maxSize = maxSize; return this; }`, next to an unchanged `public int getMaxSize()`. A loader built on `java.beans.Introspector` copies `maxSize=50` from a properties file into a new `PoolConfig` whose default is 10. What does `getMaxSize()` return afterwards?

options.text: 50, since a setter is found by its name and parameter, whatever it returns
options.says: a write method must return void; a setter that returns this is not one

options.text: 50, since a matching getter is enough to make the property writable
options.says: a getter makes the property readable only; writing needs a void setter

options.text: 10, since a setter that returns a value is not one the loader can use
options.says: the fluent setPort in the page's run gives a property with a read method and no write method

options.text: 10, since the loader writes fields directly and maxSize is private
options.says: bean tools look for methods named getX, isX and setX, not for fields

origin.section: Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean

questions.stem: A team replaces a JavaBean `Address` that had `getStreet()` and `getCity()` with `record Address(String street, String city)`. An old CSV exporter writes one column for each property that `Introspector.getBeanInfo(type, Object.class)` reports. Which columns does it write for an `Address` now?

options.text: street and city, since a record's accessor counts as the getter for its component
options.says: the introspector matches getX, isX and setX; street() matches none of them

options.text: street and city, since the introspector reads a record's components as it reads fields
options.says: the introspector doesn't read fields or components, only method names

options.text: None, since the accessors street() and city() carry no get prefix
options.says: the page's Endpoint record shows no property at all

options.text: None, since a record has no setters and a property needs both methods
options.says: a getter alone gives a read-only property, as getArea() does in the page's run

origin.section: Tools Find Properties by Method Name, and isX Works Only for a Primitive boolean

questions.stem: `record Sku(String code)` overrides its accessor: `public String code() { return code.toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT); }`. With `Object o = new Sku("ab-1")`, a `switch` on `o` with `case Sku(String c) -> log(c)` runs, and then `o.equals(new Sku("AB-1"))` is evaluated. What is logged, and what does equals return?

options.text: AB-1 is logged and equals returns true, since the pattern calls code() and the generated equals calls code() too
options.says: the generated equals compares the fields, ab-1 against AB-1

options.text: AB-1 is logged and equals returns false, since the pattern calls code() and the generated equals compares the fields
options.says: a record pattern calls the accessor; the generated equals, hashCode and toString read the fields

options.text: ab-1 is logged and equals returns false, since the pattern reads the field and the generated equals compares the fields
options.says: a record pattern calls the accessor, so it sees AB-1

options.text: ab-1 is logged and equals returns true, since the pattern reads the field and the generated equals calls code()
options.says: it is the other way round: the pattern calls the accessor and equals compares the fields

origin.section: A Record's Accessor Is name(), and Overriding It Doesn't Change equals

concepts: isX names a JavaBeans getter only when it returns a primitive boolean; Boolean isX() leaves the property without a read method.
Bean tools find properties from method names, not fields: a getter with no field behind it is a read-only property, and a setter alone a write-only one.
A record pattern calls the record's accessor, so it sees what an overridden accessor returns while equals compares the fields.
A record's accessors carry no get prefix, so java.beans.Introspector finds no property in a record.
A JavaBeans setter returns void; a fluent setter that returns this is not a write method, so tools can't set the property.
